questions.stem: Madhubani paintings originate from which region of India?
questions.explanation: Madhubani (also called Mithila) painting originates from the Mithila region of Bihar (and parts of Nepal's Janakpur). Traditionally practised by women on walls of homes during festivals; now on paper/canvas. Characterised by double-outline figures, geometric patterns, natural dyes, and themes from Hindu mythology. GI-tagged in 2007. Five distinct styles: Bharni, Kachni, Tantrik, Godna, Kohbar.

questions.stem: Warli painting, known for its simple white geometric patterns on a brown/red background, is a tribal art form of:
questions.explanation: Warli painting belongs to the Warli tribe of northern Maharashtra (Thane, Palghar districts) and southern Gujarat. Uses rice paste on mud walls — circles (sun, moon), triangles (mountains, trees), squares (human settlements), and a central 'chauk' for wedding murals. Jivya Soma Mashe (1934–2018) brought Warli to global attention. Contrast: Saora (Odisha) — similar tribal style but different motifs; Gond (MP/Chhattisgarh) — coloured dot-and-line style popularised by Jangarh Singh Shyam.

questions.stem: Pattachitra, a traditional cloth-based scroll painting, is associated with which two Indian states?
questions.explanation: Pattachitra (patta = cloth, chitra = picture) is practised in Odisha (focused on Jagannath of Puri — stylised eyes, bright colours) and West Bengal (narrative scrolls by Patua community of Medinipur). Odisha's version is GI-tagged. The art uses natural colours from minerals and plants; artists are known as 'Chitrakars'. Raghurajpur in Puri district is a heritage Pattachitra village.

questions.stem: Tanjore (Thanjavur) painting is characterised by which distinctive feature?

options.option_text: Gold foil work, glass/gem embellishments, and religious themes
Tribal stick figures with mud-based pigments
Calligraphic Arabic verses in gold script

questions.explanation: Tanjore painting originated in the 16th–18th c. under the Nayak and Maratha rulers of Thanjavur (Tamil Nadu). Distinguished by: (1) gold foil overlay (22-carat real gold leaf on raised gesso base); (2) embedded glass beads / semi-precious stones / cut-glass; (3) deities — mostly Krishna (infant Balakrishna especially) and other Hindu gods; (4) wooden plank base. GI-tagged in 2007–08. Not to be confused with Mysore painting, which lacks heavy gesso/gem work.

questions.stem: The Kangra school of miniature painting flourished primarily in which state?
questions.explanation: Kangra painting, a sub-school of Pahari miniature painting, flourished in the Kangra valley of Himachal Pradesh under Raja Sansar Chand (1775–1823). Known for lyrical depictions of Radha-Krishna themes, Gita Govinda illustrations, and delicate feminine faces with almond eyes. Pahari schools include Basohli, Guler, Kangra, Chamba, Mandi, Kulu — all in HP except Basohli (J&K). Rajasthani schools (Mewar, Marwar, Jaipur, Kishangarh, Bundi) are distinct.

questions.stem: Kalamkari, a hand-painted or block-printed cotton textile art, has two famous styles. Which two?
questions.explanation: Kalamkari (kalam = pen, kari = craft) comes from Andhra Pradesh/Telangana. The two styles: (1) SRIKALAHASTI style (Chittoor, AP) — purely hand-drawn with a bamboo pen, Hindu mythology themes; (2) MACHILIPATNAM style (Krishna district, AP) — block-printed patterns, Persian-influenced motifs. Uses natural dyes from plants + iron and mordants. GI-tagged. Vegetable block-printing survived under the Deccan Sultanate and Mughal patronage.

questions.stem: Phad painting, a narrative scroll painting traditionally of folk deities like Pabuji and Devnarayan, is from which state?
questions.explanation: Phad (or Pad) is a 700-year-old scroll painting from the Bhilwara region of Rajasthan, created on cloth ('phad' means scroll). Bhopas (traditional priest-singers) carry them village-to-village, unrolling while singing tales of local heroes Pabuji and Devnarayan. The Joshi family of Bhilwara is the hereditary custodian of the art. Uses natural dyes; dominant colour is red-orange. GI-tagged.

questions.stem: Gond painting, now globally recognised, originated as a tribal art form in which state?
questions.explanation: Gond painting comes from the Gond tribal community spread across Madhya Pradesh (Mandla, Dindori, Balaghat districts) and neighbouring regions, but is predominantly associated with MP. Characterised by intricate patterns of dots and dashes forming bright, rhythmically-filled shapes of flora, fauna, and mythology. The late Jangarh Singh Shyam (1962–2001), a Pardhan Gond from Patangarh (MP), pioneered the contemporary 'Jangarh Kalam' style and brought Gond art international recognition.

questions.stem: Which is the oldest martial art in the world, originating in Kerala?
questions.explanation: Kalaripayattu, from Kerala (dating to ~3rd c. BCE per legend; codified documentation from 13th c. CE), is widely acknowledged as one of the world's oldest surviving martial arts. 'Kalari' = training arena; 'Payattu' = fight/exercise. Four stages: Meithari (body), Kolthari (wooden weapons), Ankathari (metal weapons), Verumkai (empty hand). Three regional styles: Northern (Vadakkan), Southern (Thekkan), and Central (Madhya) — differ in stance, footwork, philosophy. Sage Parashurama is considered the mythical originator. Silambam (TN, bamboo staff), Gatka (Punjab, Sikh warrior art), Mardani Khel (Maharashtra, Maratha art) are younger.

questions.stem: Thang-Ta and Huyen Langlon are martial art traditions of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Thang-Ta ('Thang' = sword, 'Ta' = spear) and its broader philosophical framework Huyen Langlon ('method of safeguarding life') are the traditional martial arts of the Meitei people of Manipur. Practised for centuries as both warfare and ritual; revived as cultural heritage after a British ban in 1891 post the Anglo-Manipur war. Includes sword, spear, unarmed combat (Sarit Sarak), and spiritual practices. Recognised by SANG (sports body). Manipur also has Mukna (indigenous wrestling).

questions.stem: Gatka is a traditional martial art associated with which community and state?
questions.explanation: Gatka is the traditional weapon-based martial art of the Sikhs of Punjab, codified under Guru Hargobind (6th Sikh Guru, 17th c.) and refined by Guru Gobind Singh (10th Guru). It uses the 'gatka' (wooden stick simulating sword), shield, and the Khanda. Practised prominently during Hola Mohalla at Anandpur Sahib every Holi. It is both a spiritual discipline and combat system — the Nihang warrior order keeps the tradition alive. Mardani Khel is the Maratha equivalent; Chavittu Kali is another Kerala martial dance distinct from Kalaripayattu.

questions.stem: Silambam, a stick-fighting martial art using bamboo staffs, originates in which state?
questions.explanation: Silambam originates in Tamil Nadu; 'silambu' refers to the sound of the bamboo staff. It is one of the oldest South Indian martial arts (references in Sangam literature, c. 1st-4th c. CE). Used primarily the 5-6 feet bamboo stick as weapon. Kuttu Varisai is the unarmed counterpart. Today it is a recognised tournament sport under the Silambam Asia Federation. Not to be confused with Kalaripayattu (Kerala), though both are Dravidian systems.

questions.stem: Mallakhamb is a traditional gymnastic sport/martial art most famously from which state?
questions.explanation: Mallakhamb ('malla' = wrestler/strong man, 'khamb' = pole) is a Maharashtrian traditional gymnastic/martial sport where the practitioner performs yoga postures and aerial feats on a vertical wooden pole (Mallakhamb), a hanging rope (Rope Mallakhamb), or a cane (Cane Mallakhamb). Mentioned in the Manasollasa text (12th c. Chalukya). Declared Maharashtra's state sport in 2013. World Mallakhamb Championships are held in Mumbai. MP is the #2 Mallakhamb state.

questions.stem: Match the martial art to its state of origin: (1) Inbuan – (2) Sqay – (3) Cheibi Gadga – (4) Musti Yuddha
questions.explanation: INBUAN (Mizoram — belt-wrestling, similar to Kushti but on a 15-ft grass circle), SQAY (Kashmir — sword-shield fencing with leather-covered swords; internationally organised as World Sqay Federation), CHEIBI GADGA (Manipur — sword-and-shield martial art), MUSTI YUDDHA (Varanasi region of UP — ancient empty-hand boxing mentioned in the Mahabharata and Brahmanda Purana). Knowing niche state-linked martial arts is a classic SSC differentiator question.

questions.stem: Bidri (Bidriware), a metal handicraft with silver inlay on a zinc-copper alloy, has its GI tag associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Bidriware gets its name from Bidar, a city in Karnataka (formerly capital of the Bahmani Sultanate). The craft originated under the Bahmani kings in the 14th c. It is made of a zinc-copper alloy (95% Zn + 5% Cu) blackened with a paste containing soil unique to Bidar fort, then inlaid with pure silver wire. GI-tagged in 2006 (one of India's early GIs). Items: hookahs, vases, trays, jewellery boxes. Moradabad is known for brassware, not Bidri; Warangal and Kondapalli are distinct crafts.

questions.stem: Channapatna toys, known for their bright lacquer-coated wooden craft, are GI-tagged to which state?
questions.explanation: Channapatna, a small town in Karnataka's Ramanagara district, is famously known as 'Gombegala Ooru' (toy town). The craft, nearly 200 years old, uses ivory wood (Wrightia tinctoria or 'Aale mara' in Kannada), turned on lathes and lacquered with vegetable dyes. GI-tagged in 2006. Tipu Sultan invited Persian artisans who introduced the lacquer technique. Kondapalli (AP) and Thanjavur (TN) are distinct toy traditions.
